To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@aurora.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Aurora: Dec 13 throughput surge — initial data and ask

Team —

Thanks again for joining the bridge earlier. We had 3 disruption windows on Dec 13 (08:12-08:46 UTC, 14:22-14:35 UTC, 22:07-22:40 UTC). During the first window we saw a 6.2x increase in request rate to your inference endpoints and error rate spike to 11%. Latency P95 climbed from ~120ms to ~1.8s.

Attached are logs and a short summary from our side. Primary asks:
- Short RCA that we can share with our execs (by EOD tomorrow)
- Prioritized corrective actions and owners with target dates
- Confirmation on any mitigation you can push to reduce immediate risk (e.g., routing to warmed pools, temporary rate caps)

Appreciate the quick attention — this is impacting our checkout flow and our CFO is asking for a remediation timeline.

--
Amit Rao
Head of Platform Ops, Aurora Retail
amit@aurora.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Amit Rao <amit@aurora.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aurora: Dec 13 throughput surge — initial data and ask

Amit — thanks for the summary and for sending the logs. We pulled together a concise RCA and an action tracker for Aurora — attaching both here. High-level summary up front:

- Root cause: a traffic amplification pattern from a scheduled batch job on Aurora's side that caused a high-concurrency warmup to the most-used model shard; combined with suboptimal routing that briefly overloaded a small subset of GPU workers.
- Impact: intermittent 5–6x token throughput increase on affected shards; P95 latency spikes and elevated 5xx rates during the windows you noted.
- Immediate mitigations applied by Redwood: automated fallback to warmed pool (reduces P95 by ~40%), temporary per-route burst limiter, and KV cache preservation across worker churn.

What’s attached: aurora_incident_rca_20261214.pdf (full RCA) and aurora_action_tracker_20261215.xlsx (action items, owners, dates). Please see the tracker for owners and status.

Quick asks for Aurora:
- Share the schedule of the batch job and expected steady-state rates so we can tune routing heuristics
- Approve a 72-hour increased capacity budget to ride out increased load while we implement a training of the routing policy for your workload

I’ll pull a short 10–15 minute exec readout slide for your leadership unless you prefer we join your executive call?

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Attachments: aurora_incident_rca_20261214.pdf (PDF, 78KB); aurora_action_tracker_20261215.xlsx (XLSX, 34KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Amit Rao <amit@aurora.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aurora: Dec 13 throughput surge — initial data and ask

Amit / Neha — adding technical clarifications and the remediation plan from SE/infra: 

1) Cause detail: the amplification came from a spike in concurrent short requests that prevented efficient KV-cache priming on a small set of workers. When the batch fired it sent many concurrent prefixes; the runtime attempted to reallocate KV cache and evicted hot segments in the middle of inflight sessions. That led to extra recomputation and queueing.

2) Short-term fixes (today -> 72h):
   - Pin hot shards to warmed workers (deployed at 10:40 PST) — rollout confirmed.
   - Route high-concurrency prefixes to a dedicated warmed pool for Aurora (can be enabled immediately with your sign-off).
   - Enable soft throttling on the batch job’s endpoint (Aurora side) for 48–72 hours.

3) Medium-term (2–3 weeks):
   - Routing policy training for Aurora workload to avoid cross-tenant noisy neighbor effects.
   - KV cache adaptation improvement: adjust eviction policy thresholds for short-prefix-heavy workloads.

I’ve updated the tracker with engineering owners and ETA windows. Linking ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-11492

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Team + Aurora leadership — quick status and confirmation of next steps: 

- Short readout (one-pager) delivered and shared in the exec call on Dec 17. Link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/Aurora+Throughput+Surge+Dec+2026
- Immediate mitigations: pinned warmed pools and temporary soft throttling implemented (status: closed).
- Medium-term items: routing policy training scheduled; KV-cache eviction policy tuning in progress — expected completion 2027-01-05.
- Budget ask: Aurora approved a 72-hour increased capacity window; cost impact is logged in HubSpot deal D-8237.

Open items for Aurora: please share the batch job schedule and expected concurrency so Karthik’s team can finish the routing model tuning. Owners listed in the attached tracker; I’ll update HubSpot and close the loop on completed items.

Thanks all — marking this thread as the canonical incident-to-remediation thread.
